name: rkyv (zero-copy deserialization)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde (full deserialize into owned types)
verdict_reason: Zero-copy access holds: rkyv opens the log archive in about 1 ns unvalidated (292.13 µs validated) where bincode 1.3.3 needs 1.6158 ms to deserialize, and on plain-data mesh it serializes 34.7x and deserializes 25x faster. A full validated deserialize of string-heavy data is only 1.05x faster on log and slightly slower on minecraft_savedata.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark with public code; rustc nightly, the CPU and lto = true are stated.
claimed_speedup: Access log archive: 1.0914 ns unvalidated, 292.13 µs validated, vs bincode 1.3.3 deserialize 1.6158 ms. mesh: serialize 140.04 µs vs 4.8569 ms (34.7x), deserialize 144.93 µs vs 3.6395 ms (25x). log deserialize 1.2328 ms unvalidated / 1.5322 ms validated vs 1.6158 ms (1.31x / 1.05x). minecraft_savedata validated deserialize 1.5649 ms vs 1.5229 ms (slower) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: rust_serialization_benchmark log, mesh and minecraft_savedata datasets; serialize, full deserialize to owned types, and zero-copy access/read of the archived form, unvalidated and validated upfront.
toolchain: rustc 1.99.0-nightly (2026-08-06), bench profile lto = true, no target-cpu flag
one_liner: Zero-copy archive format: reads data in place in nanoseconds instead of deserializing, and serializes plain-data arrays 35x faster than bincode 1.3.
how_it_is_fast: Writes data in a layout that can be used where it lies: archived types use relative pointers, so reading a field is a cast plus offset arithmetic, not decoding. Validation is a separate upfront pass that can be skipped for trusted bytes. Plain-old-data such as float arrays is copied as-is.
use_it_when: Reading a few fields from large archives (memory-mapped files, caches) without materializing them
Plain-data-heavy payloads such as meshes or numeric arrays
Trusted data where unvalidated access is acceptable
skip_it_when: You always deserialize everything into owned types from untrusted input: the validated path was only 1.05x faster than bincode on log and slower on minecraft_savedata
You need the archived types to be your normal types; rkyv works with Archived* mirrors
Running versions before 0.8.17 on untrusted archives (see advisories)
caveats: bincode was dropped from the benchmark in 2026-08, so the comparison is from the 2026-08-07 run
Unvalidated access numbers assume trusted input; validated access is five orders of magnitude slower on log
tradeoffs: RUSTSEC-2026-0233, 0234 and 0235 (2026-05): crafted archives could pass validation and cause out-of-bounds reads or use-after-free; fixed in 0.8.17
Archives are not self-describing and are tied to the Rust type layout
